description: Each row represents a football league division, naming the division, its full name, and the country it belongs to. It links to match results for that division.

Each row represents a football match, recording the division, date, home team, away team, final goals scored by each team, and the result. It links to the divisions table for more details on the league.
Each row records the number of units sold for an item at a store on a specific date. It links to weather data by date and to sales relations by store, allowing analysis of how weather affects sales.

Each row records weather conditions at a station on a specific date. It includes temperatures (max, min, average), departure from normal, dew point, wet bulb, heat and cool indices, sunrise and sunset times, snowfall, precipitation, pressure, and wind data. It links to sales data by date and station number, allowing analysis of weather's impact on sales.
Each row records the relationship between a store and a weather station. It links a store to its corresponding weather station, allowing analysis of how weather affects sales at that store.
Each row represents a brewery, recording its unique ID, name, city, and state. It does not link to or reference any other tables.

Each row represents a beer, recording its ID, the brewery that made it, alcohol content, bitterness level, name, style, and size in ounces. It links to no other tables and is not referenced by any others.

Each row represents a batting style (how a player holds the bat) identified by an ID. It records whether the player is right-handed or left-handed. Players reference this table to indicate their preferred batting hand.
Each row represents a bowling style used in soccer, identified by a unique ID. It records the skill level associated with that bowling style. It links to players who use this bowling style.
Each row represents a city, identified by its ID and named. It records the city's associated country. Venues for matches are linked to cities through this table.
Each row represents a country, identified by its ID and named in English. It links to cities, players, and umpires to show which country they are from.

Each row represents an additional match statistic type. It records the ID and name of a specific type of extra information, such as fouls or yellow cards. It is referenced by the extra_runs table to specify what kind of extra runs were recorded.

Each row records extra runs scored in a specific ball of a match, detailing the type of extra run (like wides or no-balls), the innings number, and the exact ball within an over. It links to the match, over, ball, and extra type involved, as well as related events like wickets and scoring by batsmen.
Each row represents an outcome type in a cricket match, identified by a unique ID and named. It links to records of match outcomes and wickets taken, defining the kind of dismissal or result.
Each row represents the result of a match, noting whether it was a win, loss or draw. It records the type of outcome. This table is not linked to any other and does not reference any other table.

Each row represents a soccer player (a footballer) and includes their name, date of birth, batting hand, bowling skill, and the country they represent. It links to details about their matches, including man of the match awards, and records their performance in matches and wickets taken.

Each row defines a player's role in a match, such as goalkeeper or midfielder. It records the role ID and a description of the role. It links to the player_match table, allowing details of players' roles in specific matches.

Each row represents a soccer season, noting the man of the series and players with the most runs (orange cap) and wickets (purple cap). It records the season's year. Matches reference it to indicate which season they belong to.

Each row represents a soccer team from the 2016 season, identified by a unique ID and named. It links to matches showing which teams played against each other and who won. It also connects to players who participated in matches.
Each row records the result of a coin toss decision made before a match. It notes the unique identifier and the name of the toss. It links to matches to show which team won the toss for each game.

Each row represents a soccer referee identified by an ID. It includes the referee's name and the country they represent. It links to the country table, showing which countries have referees in the 2016 season.

Each row represents a soccer venue, including its name and the city it is located in. It links to the city table to provide more details about where each venue is situated. Joining with matches shows which venues hosted specific games.

Each row records the winning condition for a match, identified by a unique ID. It notes whether the win was by regulation time or another method like penalties. It links to matches to show which wins were decided in this way.

Each row represents a soccer match (a game) played in 2016, including the teams involved, date, venue, and outcome. It links to teams, seasons, venues, and other details like the toss winner, win type, and man of the match. Joining this table with others provides more information about each match, such as extra runs, ball by ball events, and player performances.

Each row records a ball in a cricket match, detailing the innings, teams batting and bowling, and the players involved (striker and non-striker) along with the bowler. It links to the match and additional runs data for more context.

Each row records a run scored by a batsman during an over in a specific innings of a match. It includes the runs scored and the innings number. It links to the match, over, and ball details, providing context for each run scored.

Each row represents a player's role in a match. It records the match ID, player ID, role ID, and team ID. It links to the match, player, role, and team tables, allowing details of each element to be joined for a full view of the game.

Each row records a wicket taken during a match, noting the over and ball numbers, the player dismissed, how they were out, the fielders involved, and which innings it occurred in. It links to the match, overs, balls, players, and methods of dismissal for more details.

Each row represents a city and records its country, county, and region. It links to the restaurant's general information and location details, providing context about where each restaurant is situated.

Each row contains general information about a restaurant, including its name or label, the type of food served, the city it's in, and customer reviews. It links to the city and location tables, allowing connections to specific locations within cities.

Each row represents a restaurant's location, including its street address and city. It links to the restaurant's general information and the city it is in. Joining this table provides details about where each restaurant is situated.
Each row represents an actor, including their name, date of birth, and other details like height and biography. It links to the characters table, showing which roles they played in movies.

Each row represents a movie, including its title, MPAA rating, budget, gross earnings, release date, genre, runtime, and user ratings. It links to the characters table, showing which characters are in each movie.

Each row represents a character in a movie, including which actor plays the role and their credit order. It records payment details and how much screen time the character has. It links to the movie and the actor involved, allowing connections between characters and actors across multiple movies.
Each row represents an Olympic host city, identified by a unique ID. It records the city's name. The table is linked to the games_city table, which connects it to Olympic games held there.

Each row represents an Olympic Games, identified by a unique ID. It records the year and name of the games and whether they were held during the summer or winter season. It links to the cities hosting the games and to competitors participating in them.
Each row records the host city for an Olympic Games, linking a games ID to a city ID. It connects to the games and city tables, showing which cities hosted specific Olympics.
Each row represents a type of Olympic medal (gold, silver, bronze). It records the unique identifier and the name of the medal. Competitor event results refer to it to indicate which medal was won.

Each row represents an Olympic National Olympic Committee (NOC) and its corresponding region. It records the NOC code, a short identifier, and the full region name. It links to the person_region table to associate athletes with their regions.
Each row represents an athlete, recording their ID, full name, gender, height, and weight. It links to the region where the athlete is from and to the games they competed in.

Each row records a competitor in the Olympics, noting their ID, the games they competed in, their age, and the person's ID. It links to the games and the person, and connects to events showing which competitions they participated in.
Each row links an athlete to their home region. It records the athlete's ID and the region's ID. It connects to the athlete and the NOC region, showing which athletes come from each region.
Each row represents a sport in the Olympics, identified by an ID and named. It links to events that specify which sports have competitions.

Each row represents an Olympic event, identified by a unique ID and linked to its sport. It records the event's name. The table connects to the sport table for more details on each sport and is referenced by competitor_event to link athletes to their events.

Each row records a competitor's participation in an Olympic event, linking the event, the competitor, and any medals won. It connects to events, competitors, and medals, showing which athletes competed in which events and what medals they earned.

Each row represents a language in the corpus, recording its ID, name, locale, number of pages and total word count. It links to related tables like words and biwords, allowing detailed analysis of language data.

Each row represents a page in the language corpus, recording its unique ID, the language it is written in, the page content, title, and word count. It links to languages and words associated with each page, allowing detailed analysis of text content.

Each row is a unique word in the language corpus, recording its ID, the actual word and how often it appears. It links to other tables that track word usage across different contexts and pairs of words.

Each row records how often a word appears in a language. It links to the language and the word, showing their occurrences together. Joining it with languages or words gives the frequency of each word across all languages in the corpus.

Each row records how many times a word appears on a specific page. It includes the page ID, word ID and number of occurrences. It links to the pages and words tables, allowing you to find which pages contain certain words and how often they appear.
Each row records a pair of consecutive words (biwords) in a language. It counts how often each pair occurs. The table links to the languages, and to the individual words that form the pairs.

Each row is an app available on Google Play Store. It includes the app name, category, rating, number of reviews, size, installs, type, price, content rating and genres. User reviews link to it to find which apps have been reviewed.

Each row is a user review of an app on the Google Play Store, translated into English. It includes the review text, the sentiment (positive, negative or neutral), and how positive or negative it is perceived to be, as well as its subjectivity. It links to the app being reviewed.
Each row represents a customer, with their unique identifier and names. It links to the sales table to show which sales transactions involve each customer.
Each row represents an employee, recording their unique ID, first name, middle initial, and last name. It links to the sales table to identify which sales are made by each employee.
Each row represents a product sold. It records the product's ID, name, and price. It is linked to sales transactions to show which products were sold and at what price.

Each row represents a sale, recording the unique sales ID, the salesperson, the customer, the product sold, and the quantity. It links to the salesperson, customer, and product tables, providing details of who made the sale, to whom it was made, and what was purchased.
Each row represents a video game genre, identified by an ID and named in plain text. It links to the games table to show which genres apply to each game.

Each row represents a video game, identified by an ID. It records the game's name and its genre. It links to the genre table, providing more details about the game's type. Game publishers reference this table to associate games with their publishers.
Each row represents a gaming platform (like Xbox or PlayStation). It records the platform's unique identifier and its name. The table is referenced to link games to their platforms.
Each row represents a video game publisher identified by an ID. It records the publisher's name. Other tables reference it to link games to their publishers.

Each row records the relationship between a video game and its publisher. It includes the game's ID, the publisher's ID, and links to the game and publisher tables. Joining it allows finding which games are published by each company.

Each row represents a video game on a specific platform, identified by an ID. It records the game publisher, the platform it was released on, and the release year. It links to the game publisher and the platform, and is linked from regional sales data to show sales performance.
Each row represents a game sales region, identified by an ID and named. It links to the table that records sales data for each region.
Each row records the number of sales for a video game in a specific region and on a particular platform. It links to regions and game platforms, providing details on where and how games are sold.

Each row defines a class of attributes used to describe images. It records the attribute class identifier and name. It links to image object attributes, allowing descriptions of images to be connected.
Each row defines an object class (a category of images or objects). It records the unique identifier and the name of the class. It is referenced by image objects to categorize them.

Each row represents an object in an image, identified by its image and object sample IDs. It records the object's class, position (x, y) and size (w, h). It links to additional attributes of the object and related objects in other images.

Each row is an attribute of an image object, linking it to its class and sample. It records the image ID, attribute class ID, and object sample ID. It connects to the image object table for details on the image and to the attribute classes table for the type of attribute.

Each row defines a prediction class, which is a category used for image recognition. It records the class ID and description of the class. This table connects to another through the class ID, allowing classification results to be linked to specific categories.

Each row represents a relationship between image objects, identified by the image ID, prediction class ID, and two object sample IDs. It links to images and their predicted classes, showing how objects are related in an image.

Each row represents demographic data for a geographic area, including the number of inhabitants and income. It also includes 18 unnamed variables. It links to customer data by geographic ID, helping to understand customer demographics.
Each row records a mailing to a customer or prospect, noting the reference ID, date of the mailing, and the recipient's response. It links to related tables for more details on responses and sales.

Each row represents a customer of the software company. It records the customer's sex, marital status, geographic location, education level, occupation and age. It links to demographic data for more details on the customer’s location.

Each row records a mailing reference, including its date and the recipient's response. It links to related mailings for more details and is linked from those same records to connect responses across multiple mailings.
Each row represents a sales event, recording the date and amount of a sale. It includes an event ID and a reference ID linking to related mailings.

Each row represents an author, with their unique ID and name. It also records the author's affiliation (where they are from or work). Papers reference this table to link authors to their publications.
Each row represents a conference, with its unique ID, short name, full name and home page URL. It links to papers that were presented at the conference.
Each row represents a scientific journal, with its ID, short name, full name and home page URL. It links to papers published in the journal.

Each row is a research paper, with its ID, title, year of publication, and keywords. It links to the conference or journal where it was published, and records which authors contributed (via another table).

Each row records an author of a research paper, noting their name and the institution they are affiliated with. It links to the papers and authors tables, connecting multiple authors to a single paper.

Each row represents a country identified by an ISO code. It records the country's ID, its ISO code, and its full name. The production_country table references it to link movies to their countries of origin.

Each row represents a production department involved in making a movie, such as cinematography or sound. It records the department's unique ID and its name. It links to the crew members assigned to each department.
Each row represents a gender (e.g., male, female). It records the gender ID and the gender description. This table is referenced to determine the gender of actors in movies.
Each row represents a movie genre, identified by an ID and named in plain text. It links to the table that associates genres with movies.
Each row is a keyword used to describe a movie, identified by a unique ID. It records the text of the keyword. The table is referenced by movie_keywords to link movies to their keywords.
Each row represents a movie language, identified by an ID. It records the language's code and its full name. The table is referenced to list languages for movies.

Each row represents a language role in a movie, such as the original language or dubbed version. It records the role's ID and description. The table is referenced to link languages to their roles in movies.

Each row represents a movie, including its title, budget, release date, and popularity. It also records the revenue, runtime, status, tagline, and ratings (average vote and number of votes). This table connects to other tables that detail genres, languages, crew, production countries, cast, keywords, and companies involved in making the movie.
Each row records the genres of a movie, linking movies to their genres. It connects through movie_id and genre_id to the movie and genre tables.
Each row records the languages a movie is available in and their roles. It links to the movie, the language, and the language role, connecting details about multilingual releases.

Each row represents a person involved in making or appearing in movies. It records the person's unique identifier and their name. It links to tables that detail their roles as crew members or cast in specific films.
Each row records a crew member's role in making a movie, including their job title. It links to the movie, the person and the department they worked in.
Each row represents a movie production company identified by a unique ID. It records the company's name. Other tables link to it to show which movies were produced by each company.
Each row records the production country of a movie, linking it to both the movie and the country. It shows which countries produced specific movies.
Each row represents a cast member in a movie, including their character name and the order of appearance. It links to the movie, the person playing the role, and the character's gender.

Each row links a movie to one of its keywords. It records the movie's ID and the keyword's ID, without additional details about the keyword or movie. It connects movies to their tags through the keyword table.
Each row records the relationship between a movie and its production company. It links to the movie and the company involved in making it.
Each row represents a location, identified by an ID. It records the country, state, state code, and city. Twitter user locations reference this table to link users to their geographic information.
Each row represents a user on the social media platform. It records the user's ID and gender. The table is linked to Twitter user data, allowing cross-referencing with specific Twitter accounts.

Each row represents a Twitter tweet, including its ID, weekday and hour of posting, language, whether it's a reshare, reach count, retweets, likes, Klout score, sentiment analysis, text content, location ID, and user ID. It links to the location and user tables for more details.
Each row represents a company location, including its city, address, state, zip code and phone number. It links to the employees who work at that location.
Each row represents a job position within the company, including its ID, title, required education level, and minimum and maximum salaries. It links to employees who hold these positions.

Each row represents an employee, recording their social security number, name, hire date, salary, gender, performance rating, and the position and location they work in. It links to the position and location tables, providing details about each employee's role and workplace.
Each row represents a customer, identified by their ID. It holds the customer's name. This table is linked from sales orders to connect them to their customers.
Each row represents a product sold. It records the product ID and name. It is referenced by sales orders to track which products were sold.
Each row represents a state and its assigned region. It records the state code, name of the state, and the region it belongs to. It links to store locations to show which stores are in each region.

Each row represents a sales team and its assigned region. It records the unique identifier, name of the sales team, and the region it covers. It links to sales orders to show which teams are responsible for which orders.

Each row represents a store location, including its city name, state code, and geographic details like latitude and longitude. It also includes demographic data such as population and income levels. This table links to the states in which stores are located and is referenced by sales orders to connect them to specific stores.

Each row is a sales order, recording details like the order number, date of purchase and delivery, currency, and quantities. It links to the sales team, customer, store, and product involved, providing a full picture of each sale.

Each row represents a computer science course. It records the course's ID and its level (e.g., beginner, intermediate, advanced). It links to the instructor who teaches the course and is linked from the taughtby table to show which courses instructors teach.

Each row represents a person, either a professor or a student. It records their position, phase of the program, and how long they have been in the program. It links to show who advises whom and which courses are taught by each person.

Each row records the advising relationship between two people. It links a student to their advisor, identified by person IDs. This table connects to the person table twice for redundancy and is referenced back to it.

Each row records that a person teaches a course. It links to the course and the teacher, showing which courses are taught by whom. Joining it with other tables can show the teaching schedule or faculty assignments.

Each row represents a country or region, identified by a code. It records the name of the country/region and when its data was last modified. It links to other tables that reference it, such as currency information, sales territories, and states/provinces.

Each row represents a cultural category used to describe products. It records the culture's ID, its name and when it was last modified. It links to and from tables that use these categories to describe product models and descriptions.

Each row represents a currency, identified by its code. It records the currency's name and when it was last updated. It links to the table that associates currencies with countries, allowing you to see which currencies are used where.

Each row represents the currency used in a country or region. It records the country/region code, currency code, and the date when this information was last updated. It links to the country/region and currency tables, allowing you to see which currencies are used where.

Each row represents a person (an individual or entity) in the organization. It includes details like name, title, email preferences, and contact information. It links to other tables such as business entities, emails, employees, and customers, providing a comprehensive record of each person's data.

Each row represents a contact method for a business entity (such as an employee or supplier) and the person associated with it. It records the business entity ID, person ID, contact type ID, a unique identifier, and when the record was last modified. It links to the business entity, the person, and the contact type, allowing you to see all contacts for a given entity or person.
Each row is an email address associated with a business entity. It records the email address, its unique identifier and when it was last modified. It links to the person who owns the email address.

Each row represents an employee, including their ID, login details, organizational information, job title, personal data like birthdate and gender, hire date, and leave balances. It links to the person table for more detailed personal information and is referenced by salesperson and purchase order header tables.
Each row stores a user's password details, including the business entity ID, password hash, salt, unique identifier and last modification date. It links to the person table to identify the user.

Each row records a credit card linked to a person. It includes the person's ID and the credit card's ID, with the date of any modifications. It links to the person and the credit card, and is referenced in sales orders that use these cards.

Each row represents a product category, identified by an ID. It includes the category's name, a unique identifier, and the last modification date. The ProductCategory table is referenced by the productsubcategory table to define broader categories for products.

Each row describes a product, including its ID, description, unique identifier, and last modification date. It links to the product model description culture table, providing details on how products are described in different cultures.
Each row represents a product model, with its ID, name, catalog description, and instructions. It links to related descriptions in other languages and to products that use this model.

Each row represents a product description in a specific language, linking a product model to its description and the language used. It records the modified date of each description. This table connects to other tables for product models, descriptions, and cultures, allowing detailed views of products across different languages.
Each row is a product photograph, including its thumbnail and large versions. It records the photo filenames and when the photo was last modified. It links to and from the product it photographs.
Each row represents a product subcategory, identified by its ID and named. It links to the product category it belongs to and is linked from products that fall under this subcategory.

Each row is a reason for a sales adjustment, identified by a unique ID. It records the name of the reason, its type and when it was last modified. It links to and from sales order header records that use these reasons.

Each row represents a sales territory, including its name, country region code, and year-to-date and last-year sales and costs. It links to the country region and is connected to salespeople, customers, states/provinces, and sales orders, showing which territories they belong to or operate in.

Each row represents a salesperson and includes their unique identifier, territories they manage, sales quotas, bonuses, commission rate, year-to-date and last-year sales figures. It links to the employee table for identification and to the territory table for assigned regions. Joining it with other tables provides historical quota data and store assignments.

Each row records a sales quota assigned to a salesperson on a specific date. It includes the quota amount, the date it was set, and when it was last modified. It links to the salesperson who received the quota.

Each row records the sales territory a business entity (likely a salesperson) was assigned to, along with start and end dates. It links to the salesperson, the territory, and various history tables, showing changes in assignments over time.

Each row is a reason for scrap (why a product was scrapped or rejected). It records the scrap reason's ID, its name and when it was last updated. It links to work orders that record instances of this scrap reason being used.
Each row represents a work shift, recording its ID, name, start time, end time and last modification date. It links to employee department history records, showing which shifts employees worked.

Each row defines a shipping method used for orders. It records the method's name, base cost, per-item rate, and tracking details. This table is referenced by both purchase and sales order headers to determine shipping costs and methods.

Each row represents a special offer or promotion, including its ID, description, discount percentage, type, category, start and end dates, minimum and maximum quantities. It links to the products that benefit from the offer and to historical sales territories where it was active.

Each row represents an address associated with a business entity, linking the entity to its mailing or billing address. It includes details like the address type and when it was last modified. It connects to the business entity and the specific address type used.
Each row is a sales tax rate for a specific state or province. It records the tax type, rate, and other identifying information like the name. It links to the state or province it applies to.

Each row represents a store, identified by its business entity ID. It includes the store's name, the salesperson in charge, and demographic information. It links to the salesperson and connects to customers associated with it.

Each row records a reason for a sales order modification. It includes the sales order ID and the sales reason ID, with the date when it was last modified. It links to sales orders and sales reasons, connecting them to show why orders were changed.

Each row is a historical record of a transaction, detailing changes in product quantities and costs. It includes the transaction ID, product ID, order reference details, date, type, quantity, actual cost, and modification date. It links to the current product cost history and is referenced by active transaction records for updates.

Each row defines a unit of measure (like grams or liters) used in the business. It records the code, name and last modified date of each unit. It is referenced by tables for products and bills of materials to specify units used.

Each row records the standard cost of a product over time, starting from a specific date. It includes the start and end dates, the standard cost, and when the record was last modified. It links to the product and other historical sales data, allowing you to track cost changes and related transactions.

Each row is a document associated with a product, recording the product's ID and the node of the document. It links to the product and another document, showing which documents relate to each product.

Each row represents the inventory of a product at a specific location within a warehouse. It records the product ID, shelf, bin, and quantity. It links to the product and location details, allowing you to see where each product is stored.

Each row is a photo associated with a product. It records whether the photo is primary and when it was last modified. It links to the product and its photo, allowing you to see which photos belong to each product and which products have specific photos.

Each row is a product review, recording the reviewer's name, review date, email address, rating and comments. It links to the product being reviewed, allowing you to see all reviews for a specific item.

Each row is an item in a shopping cart, recording the quantity and product details. It includes the cart's ID, the date it was created and last modified. It links to the product for more information on what is being bought.

Each row represents a special offer for a product. It records the special offer ID, product ID, a unique identifier (rowguid), and when it was last modified. It links to the special offers and products tables, allowing you to see which products are offered with each special deal and how they appear in sales details.

Each row details an item in a sales order, including the quantity ordered, product and special offer IDs, unit price, discount, and line total. It links to the main sales order, the product, and the special offer, providing a breakdown of each order.

Each row is a record of a transaction in the works cycles database, detailing changes to products. It includes the transaction ID, product ID, reference order and line IDs, date, type, quantity, actual cost, and modification date. It links to an archive for historical data and connects back to products.

Each row represents a vendor (a supplier of goods or services). It includes details like the account number, name, credit rating, and whether it is a preferred vendor. It links to other tables for purchasing web service URLs and modifications history, and connects to products that use its vendors and purchase orders.

Each row represents a product-vendor relationship, recording the average lead time, standard price, and other details like minimum and maximum order quantities. It links to the product, vendor, and unit measure tables, allowing for detailed inventory management.

Each row is a purchase order header, recording details of an order placed by the company. It includes information like the order ID, revision number, status, employee and vendor involved, shipping method, dates, amounts, and modifications. It links to employees, vendors, and shipping methods, and connects to the items ordered in the detail table.

Each row details an item in a purchase order, including the due date, quantity ordered, unit price, and quantities received, rejected, and stocked. It links to the purchase order header and the product, showing the order's status and modifications over time.

Each row represents a work order (a production task) for manufacturing a product. It records the product ID, quantity ordered and stocked, scrapped, start and end dates, due date, scrap reason, and last modified date. It links to related tables like work order routing, products, sales territory history, and scrap reasons, allowing detailed tracking of production tasks.

Each row represents a step in the production process of a specific product order. It records the scheduled and actual start and end dates, resource hours, costs, and location for each operation. It links to the work order, product, and location involved, allowing tracking of production details.

Each row represents a customer, identified by a unique ID. It includes details like the person associated with the account, the store they are linked to, their sales territory, and other identifying information such as an account number. It links to related tables for more detailed information on people, stores, and territories, and is referenced by sales transactions to connect customers to their orders.

Each row records a historical price change for a product. It includes the product ID, start and end dates of the price period, the list price, and when the record was last modified. It links to products and sales territory history, allowing connections between price changes and territories.

Each row represents an address, including the street lines, city, state, postal code, and spatial location. It links to the state or province and is linked from tables that store business entity addresses.

Each row defines an address type (such as "home" or "work"). It records the type's name, a unique identifier and the date it was last modified. It links to and is referenced from the businessentityaddress table, which connects addresses to entities.

Each row describes a component in a product assembly, including the start and end dates of its use, the unit of measure, the level in the bill of materials hierarchy, and the quantity per assembly. It links to sales territory history for date ranges and to unit measure definitions.

Each row represents a business entity (such as a person or organization) identified by a unique ID. It includes a GUID for tracking and the date when it was last modified. It links to other tables like contacts, addresses, stores, and vendors, connecting them back to this core entity.

Each row defines a type of contact (such as email or phone). It records the contact type's name and when it was last changed. It links to and is linked from tables that record specific contacts for business entities.

Each row represents a currency exchange rate on a specific date. It records the rates for converting between two currencies, including average and end-of-day rates. It links to sales orders to determine the currency conversion rates used in those transactions.

Each row represents a department in the organization. It records the department's ID, name, group it belongs to, and when it was last modified. It links to employee-department history, showing which employees worked in this department.

Each row records an employee's history of working in a specific department and shift, including the start and end dates. It links to the person (employee), department, and shift involved, showing when and where they worked.

Each row represents a book publisher, identified by an ID and its name. It links to books that it publishes, showing which publishers are involved in the collection.

Each row represents a delivery truck, identified by its ID. It records the truck's make and model year. It links to shipments to show which trucks are used for deliveries.

Each row represents a food business, including its name, address, and contact details. It records the business certificate, application date, and owner information. This table links to inspection results and violation records for each business.

Each row records a rating for a movie, including the rating score and timestamp. It links to the movie being rated and to the user who gave the rating. It also includes details about the critic or user providing the feedback.
Each row represents a chapter in one of Shakespeare's works, detailing an act and scene. It includes a brief description and links the chapter to its corresponding work.

Each row represents an author with their last and first names, contact information, and a contract status. It links to the titleauthor table, which records which authors wrote which books.

Each row represents a book publisher, including their name and location details. It links to additional publisher information and is linked from employees and books they publish.

Each row contains information about a publisher, including their logo and contact details. It links to the main publishers table and is referenced from it.

Each row represents a store that sells books. It records the store's name, address, city, state, and ZIP code. It links to other tables like sales and discounts, allowing connections to track sales and discount activities at each store.
Each row defines a discount type for books, specifying the store ID, the range of quantities eligible for the discount, and the discount percentage. It links to the store that offers the discount.

Each row records a miscellaneous hockey award, including the awardee's name, the specific award, the year it was given, and any notes. It links to the league and team associated with the award, and connects to the Hall of Fame and team tables for further details.

Each row represents an officer involved in a shooting incident. It includes the officer's race, gender, last and first names, and a full name. It links to the incidents table using the case number.

Each row represents a person involved in an incident, identified by their race, gender, and full name. It links to the incidents table using the case number, providing details of individuals related to shooting cases.

Each row represents a customer, including their ID, name, and address details like country, city, state, and postal code. It also notes the customer's segment and region. This table connects to regions for product segmentation and is linked to various store-specific tables by customer ID and region.

Each row represents a product sold in the superstore. It records the product name, category, and sub-category. The table links to regions, allowing you to see which products are available in each area. It connects to multiple stores that stock these products.

Each row represents an order placed at the superstore, including details like order date, ship date, customer ID, region, product ID, sales amount, quantity sold, discount given, and profit. It links to other tables for more detailed information on customers, regions, and products. Joining it with these tables provides a comprehensive view of each sale.

Each row represents an order from the east region of the superstore. It records details like order date, ship date, customer ID, product ID, sales amount, quantity, discount and profit. It links to the central superstore for additional data, to customers for their information, to regions for location, and to products for more details.

Each row represents a sales order from the south region of the superstore. It records the order date, ship date, ship mode, customer ID, product ID, and financial details like sales, quantity, discount, and profit. It links to central superstore data, customer information, product details, and regional areas.

Each row represents a sales order from the west region of the superstore. It records the order date, ship date, ship mode, customer ID, product ID, and financial details like sales, quantity, discount, and profit. It links to central superstore data, customer information, product details, and regional areas.
Each row represents a user of the movie rating system. It records the user's age, gender, and occupation. It links to and is referenced from another table that stores base user information.

Each row represents a movie director, noting their quality rating and average revenue from their films. It links to the movies2directors table, which records the relationship between directors and movies.
Each row represents an actor, noting their gender and quality rating. It links to the movies2actors table, which records the actors in each movie.

Each row represents a movie, with details like its ID, release year, language, country of origin, and running time. It links to actors, directors, and user ratings, allowing connections between movies and their creative teams or viewers.

Each row records an actor's role in a movie, noting the actor and movie IDs along with their casting order. It links to the movies and actors tables, allowing you to see which actors were in which films and vice versa.

Each row records the relationship between a movie and its director, including the movie's genre. It links to the movies and directors tables, allowing you to find all movies directed by a specific director or all directors of a particular movie.

Each row records a user's rating of a movie. It includes the user ID, movie ID and the rating given. It links to the users who rated and the movies they rated, allowing connections between users and their ratings.

Each row represents a customer, noting their CustomerID, the client segment they belong to, and the currency used in their transactions. It links to transaction data and monthly summaries of activity.
Each row represents a gas station, identified by its Gas Station ID. It records the station's Chain ID, the Country it operates in, and its chain segment. It links to transaction data for analysis.

Each row represents a product (likely a type of debit card). It records the product's ID and its description. It is referenced by transactions that record which products are involved in financial transactions.

Each row is a transaction (a debit card purchase). It records the transaction ID, date and time, customer ID, card ID, gas station ID, product ID, amount, and price. It links to the year-month of the date, the customer who made the purchase, the gas station where it occurred, and the product bought.

Each row records a customer's debit card usage for a specific month and year. It includes the customer ID, the date of transaction, and the amount consumed. It links to the customer and is linked from the transactions table, showing monthly spending patterns.

Each row represents a financial account, identified by an account ID. It records the location of the branch, how often transactions occur, and the date. It links to the district where the branch is located and connects to tables for dispenses, loans, orders, and transactions related to the account.
Each row is a credit card, identified by its ID. It records the card's disposition ID, type and issue date. It links to the card's disposition details.

Each row represents a financial client, recording their gender and birth date. It also notes the location of the branch serving them. It links to the district for more details on where the client is located.

Each row is a disposition (a financial action or decision) for a client's account. It records the type of action and links to the client and account involved. Cards refer to it to show which actions are associated with an account.

Each row represents a district, including its location, name, region, population details, economic and social data like unemployment rates and crime statistics. It links to accounts and clients associated with that district.
Each row represents a loan, recording the loan ID, associated account, loan date, total amount, repayment duration, monthly payments, and current status. It links to the account linked to the loan.

Each row represents a financial order or transaction. It records the account from which money is debited, the recipient's bank and account details, the amount transferred, and a characterization of the payment. It links to the account that is debited.

Each row is a financial transaction, recording details like the transaction ID, date, type (+ or -), operation mode, amount, and resulting balance. It links to the account involved and shows the partner's bank and account.

Each row represents a Formula 1 race circuit, including its ID, name, location, and coordinates. It provides details like the country and URL for more information. This table is referenced by the races table to link circuits to their respective races.

Each row represents a Formula 1 team, identified by a unique ID. It includes the team's reference name, full name, nationality, and URL. This table is referenced by other tables to link race results, standings, and qualifying sessions to teams.

Each row represents a Formula 1 driver, including their ID, name (forename and surname), number, date of birth, nationality, and URL. It links to tables recording lap times, driver standings, pit stops, qualifying sessions, and race results, connecting these data points back to the driver.
Each row represents a Formula 1 racing season, identified by the race year. It includes a URL for more details. The season links to individual races held that year.

Each row represents a Formula 1 race, including its ID, year, round number, circuit ID, name, date, and time. It links to circuits for the venue details and seasons for the year category. Joining it provides information on lap times, pit stops, qualifying results, constructors' standings, drivers' standings, and final results.

Each row records a constructor's result in a race, including the points scored and the final status of the car. It links to the race and the constructor involved, providing details of each team's performance.

Each row shows a constructor's (team's) standing after a race, including points scored, position in the standings, and number of wins. It links to the race and the constructor, connecting them to show performance over races.
Each row shows a driver's standing after a race, including points, position, and wins. It links to the race and the driver involved, providing detailed standings information.

Each row records a driver's lap time during a race. It includes the race ID, driver ID, lap number, position, and time in milliseconds. It links to the race and driver tables, providing details of each driver’s performance per lap.

Each row records a pit stop during a Formula 1 race for a specific driver. It includes the stop number, lap number, time taken and duration in milliseconds. It links to the race, driver, and lap times, providing details of each pit stop.

Each row records a qualifying session result for a driver in a Formula 1 race. It includes the position, and times from each of the three qualifying rounds. It links to the race, driver, and constructor, providing details on who qualified and how well they did.
Each row represents a race status (such as retired or finished). It records the status ID and description. The results table links to it to show the final status of each car in a race.
Each row represents a driver's result in a Formula 1 race, including their position, time, and other details like fastest lap. It links to the race, driver, constructor, and status for more context.

Each row represents a school in California, detailing its free and reduced-price meal program. It includes information like the academic year, county and district codes, school name, enrollment numbers, and percentage of students eligible for free or reduced-price meals. It links to the main schools table, allowing for more detailed queries about each school.

Each row contains SAT score data for a school, including the school's name, district and county. It records enrollment, number of test takers, average scores in reading, math, and writing, and the number of high-scoring students. It links to the schools table using the cds code.

Each row represents a school in California, including its identification numbers, location, contact information, status, ownership details, and educational offerings. It records key details like the school's address, phone number, website, opening and closing dates, and whether it is virtual or a magnet school. The table connects to other tables through the CDSCode, allowing for related data such as financial data and test scores to be linked.

Each row represents a card from a card game, identified by a unique ID. It includes details like the artist, name, availability, color identity, mana cost, and various other attributes such as flavor text and alternative deck limits. This table connects to other tables through foreign keys for legalities and rulings.

Each row contains foreign flavor text or card text from a card game. It records the card's multiverse ID, its name, type, and the text in different languages. It links to the main cards table using the UUID.
Each row records the legality of a game format, noting its status. It includes a unique identifier for linking to related card data.

Each row represents a card game set, including its base and total size, block or booster status, and release date. It also includes identifiers for marketplaces like Magic Card Market and TCG Player. These sets are referenced by translations that provide localized names.

Each row is a translation of a card game set name into another language. It includes the translation ID, the language, the set code and the translated name. It links to the card game set, allowing you to see all translations for a particular set.
Each row is a ruling or official interpretation for a card in a game, recorded with its date and text. It links to the card via its UUID, allowing rulings to be matched to specific cards.

Each row represents a set of attributes for a football player at a specific date. It includes ratings for various skills like passing, dribbling, and physical attributes such as stamina and strength. It links to the player table using their unique IDs, allowing you to track a player's development over time.

Each row represents a football player, including their ID, API identifiers, name, birthday, height, and weight. It links to other tables that track player attributes and match details, allowing for comprehensive player information across various contexts.
Each row represents a football league, identified by an ID and named after its country. It links to the country where the league is based.
Each row represents a country in European football. It records the country's unique ID and its name. The table is referenced by the league table to specify which countries have football leagues.

Each row represents a football team, including its unique ID, long and short names. It also includes API IDs for FIFA and other services. This table is referenced by tables tracking team attributes and match results.

Each row represents a set of attributes for a football team, including their build-up play speed and passing accuracy. It also includes details on chance creation and defensive strategies. These attributes are recorded on specific dates and linked to the team through its FIFA API ID and team API ID.

Each row represents a match in a European football league, including the date, teams involved, goals scored, and players on the field. It records detailed information about both home and away teams and their players. This table connects to team and player tables to provide full details of each match.

Each row represents an examination for potential thrombosis, recording various antibody levels and coagulation measures. It also notes the patient's symptoms and diagnosis. It links to the patient who underwent the examination.

Each row represents a patient with potential thrombosis issues. It includes the patient's sex, birthday, description, first date of concern, admission details and diagnosis. It links to related examinations and laboratory results for further information.

Each row represents a laboratory test result for a patient at a specific date. It includes various blood and urine tests such as AST, ALT, LDH, ALP, protein levels, glucose, white blood cells, red blood cells, platelets, and clotting factors. It links to the patient record by ID, allowing correlation of test results with individual patients.

Each row represents an atom in a chemical molecule, identified by its type (element) and linked to the molecule it belongs to. It connects to other atoms within the same molecule and records their relationships.

Each row describes a chemical bond between atoms in a molecule. It records the bond's unique ID, the molecule it belongs to, and its type (e.g., single, double). It links to the molecule table and connects to other bonds within the same molecule.

Each row represents a connection between two atoms in a chemical structure, identified by their atom IDs and a bond ID. It links to the atoms involved and to the bonds connecting them, showing how atoms are connected within molecules.

Each row represents a chemical molecule identified by a unique ID. It contains the molecule's label or name. This table is referenced by tables that describe atoms and bonds within molecules, linking back to identify which molecule each atom or bond belongs to.
Each row represents a club event, recording its name, date, type, additional notes, location, and status. It links to records of who attended the event and to the event's budget.

Each row represents a major (a field of study) in the student club. It records the major's name, the associated department and college. The table is linked to members who are enrolled in these majors, allowing queries about which students are studying each major.
Each row is a zip code entry, recording the type of area, city, county, and state. It links to members who are associated with that zip code.
Each row records a student's attendance at an event. It links the event and the student. Joining it to other tables shows which students attended which events and vice versa.

Each row represents a budget allocation for an event, recording the category, amount allocated, amount spent and remaining balance. It links to the event it relates to and connects to expenses that record actual spending.
Each row records an expense (cost incurred) for a student club, including the description, date, and cost. It links to the member who approved it and to the budget it relates to.
Each row records an income received by the student club, noting the date, amount, source and any additional notes. It links to the member who is associated with the income.

Each row represents a club member, recording their name, contact information, position in the club and size of t-shirt. It links to the member's zip code and major, and connects to tables tracking attendance, expenses and income.

Each row represents a superhero's alignment (good, bad or neutral). It records the unique ID and the description of the alignment. The superhero table references it to specify each hero's moral stance.
Each row represents a superhero attribute, such as power or weakness. It records the attribute's name. It is linked to the hero_attribute table, which connects attributes to superheroes.
Each row represents a colour used to describe superheroes. It records the colour's ID and name. It links to the superhero table for eye, hair, and skin colours.
Each row represents a gender (male, female, or other). It records the gender's ID and description. The superhero table references it to specify each hero's gender.
Each row represents a comic book publisher. It records the publisher's name and an identifier. Superheroes are linked to this table to show which publisher created them.
Each row represents a superhero race or type. It records the race's ID and name. The race table is referenced by the superhero table to indicate each hero's race.

Each row represents a superhero, including their name, full identity, gender, eye and hair color, skin color, race, publisher, alignment, height, and weight. It links to tables for gender, colors, races, publishers, alignments, and attributes or powers, providing a comprehensive profile of each superhero.

Each row records an attribute of a superhero, such as their superpower or weakness. It links to the superhero and the specific attribute, allowing details like strength level or ability type to be stored.
Each row describes a superpower, identified by an ID. It records the name of the power. Other tables link to it to show which heroes have which powers.
Each row records a power or ability that a superhero possesses. It links to the superhero and the specific power, showing which heroes have which abilities.
Each row is a badge awarded to a user, identified by an ID. It records the user's ID, the badge name and the date it was awarded. It links to the user who received the badge.
Each row is a comment on a post, recording its score, text, and creation date. It links to the post it comments on and to the user who posted it.
Each row records a change to a post in the community, including its type, date, user, and any text or comment added. It links to the post and the user who made the change.

Each row links one post to another, indicating a relationship between them. It records the creation date, the IDs of both posts and the type of link. It connects to other posts through their IDs, showing which posts are related.

Each row is a post (a question or answer) in the community forum. It includes details like creation date, score, body text, and user information such as owner and last editor. It links to users for ownership and editing details, and connects to related tables for comments, edits, and voting.
Each row is a tag used to categorize content, with its name, usage count and associated excerpt post ID. It links to the excerpt of the post it describes.

Each row represents a user in the community, including their reputation, creation date, display name, and other details like location and about me. It links to other tables that track badges, comments, post history, and voting activity for each user.
Each row records a vote on a post, including the type of vote, when it was cast and who voted. It links to the post and the user making the vote.
